title: Roo and Nuzzle Help a Friend
markdown:
Roo the kangaroo and his best friend Nuzzle the koala toy lived in a bright sunny field. Nuzzle was soft, like a fluffy cloud you can hug. Roo loved to hop. And Nuzzle, all snug in Roo’s pouch, loved to hop too.

Today was a special day. Roo had a bright yellow note with a big red heart for Mrs. Wombat. She makes the yummiest berry muffins. Roo wanted to put the note in the mailbox at the end of the path.

“Come on, Nuzzle. Mailbox job.”

The path had pretty flowers, like little nodding heads. Roo hopped past busy ants walking in a line.

“Hello, ants,” he called.

The ants wiggled their feelers back.

Then Mr. Badger, stripey nose, digging.

“Good morning, Mr. Badger.”

Mr. Badger gave a happy grunt. Saying hello made Roo and Nuzzle feel warm and happy.

Suddenly Roo stopped hopping. He heard a tiny little sound. It sounded lost. Roo hopped closer to a big green leaf. And there she was: a teeny-tiny ladybug. Her bright red shell wasn’t shiny. She wiggled her little legs sadly.

“Oh, hello,” said Roo softly. Nuzzle snuggled closer. “We’re here to help.”

The ladybug looked up.

“I can’t find my way home,” she whispered. Her voice was like a little sad bell. “I hid too well when we played.”

Roo’s big bouncy heart went thump-thump-thump.

“Don’t worry. We can help.”

Roo looked all around. He saw bright pink flowers a little way off, near a little brook.

“Are your friends there?” he asked, pointing. “Those pink flowers smell so sweet.”

The ladybug wiggled her feelers. A little bit of hope came.

“Oh. Yes. My friends love the pink flowers.”

Roo carefully bent down. Nuzzle peeked out.

“Hop on this,” Roo said gently, nudging a soft grass blade. Then, instead of big hops, Roo did little gentle hops. He carried the ladybug safely to the pink flowers. She held on tight, her spots looking like shiny candies.

A whole bunch of ladybugs came running out.

“Daisy! You’re back!” they cheered.

The little ladybug, Daisy, wiggled with happiness. Her shell shone bright.

“Thank you, Roo. Thank you, Nuzzle,” Daisy chirped. Her voice was like a happy bell. “You are very kind friends.”

Roo felt a happy wiggle in his tummy. Helping Daisy felt even better than muffins.

“You’re welcome.”

Then Roo remembered.

“We still need to get to the mailbox, Nuzzle. Have fun playing, Daisy. Bye-bye.”

With a wave to Daisy and her happy ladybug family, Roo started to hop again. He hopped past the ants. He hopped past Mr. Badger. The sun felt warm.

Finally they saw it: the big blue mailbox. Roo hopped right up to it. With a little wiggle he popped the bright yellow note inside. It was in. Click.

Roo did a happy dance, twirling.

“We did it, Nuzzle. We delivered the thank-you note.”

Nuzzle swayed, all warm and cozy. They did not decide that delivering a note and helping a new friend was the very best kind of adventure of all. Roo only patted the mailbox once, felt Nuzzle’s soft cloud-fur against his pouch, and hopped home the long way so the pink flowers could keep cheering Daisy without him, the yellow note already safe for Mrs. Wombat’s muffins.
